key_insight: A single mixed audio stream can be converted into synchronized, co-located 3D facial animations for two interacting people by explicitly modeling their spatial relationship (relative position, orientation, and mutual gaze), producing far more realistic in-person dialogues than independent talking-head generation.
problem_solved: Generates complete, spatially-aware 3D animations for two co-located participants from a mixed audio input—addressing the lack of mutual gaze, correct orientation, and realistic spatial interaction in prior multi-person audio-to-animation methods.
method: Audio-driven separation & attribution: disentangle mixed audio to identify per-speaker signals and timing.
Spatial-aware 3D synthesis: predict each participant’s 3D head/face motion along with relative position and orientation so interactions reflect in-person geometry.
Joint optimization for social cues: enforce mutual gaze, turn-taking, and orientational consistency so both avatars behave coherently during dialogue.
impact: Enables more realistic multi-person avatars for telepresence, VR/AR, social robotics, and dataset generation—improving immersive communication and downstream tasks that require believable interpersonal dynamics.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: mixed audio → speaker attribution → spatial reasoning → dual 3D animation output
Before/after comparison: conference-style side-by-side with synthesized co-located interaction (showing gaze and orientation differences)
Spatial schematic: top-down view with relative positions, orientation arrows, and gaze vectors between two avatars
Evaluation summary: compact bar/metric chart or user study snapshot highlighting realism and interaction quality gains
paper_title: Talking Together: Synthesizing Co-Located 3D Conversations from Audio
paper_authors: Mengyi Shan, Shouchieh Chang, Ziqian Bai, Shichen Liu, Yinda Zhang
